en.headline: Woman reports HK$21.5 million lost in crypto scam
en.dek: Police said a 60-year-old woman reported transfers between April and September after a site asked for a deposit to prove her account was clean.
body: Police received a report on Saturday from a 60-year-old woman who said she had lost about HK$21.5 million in an online cryptocurrency investment, Hong Kong 01 and Oriental Daily reported.

According to the reports, she met someone claiming to be an investment expert on an online platform and was later drawn onto a virtual site to invest in cryptocurrency. The site then asked her to pay a deposit to show the account was not being used for money laundering. She made multiple transfers to designated accounts between 14 April and 22 September, and reported the case after she suspected she had been deceived.

Police classified the case as obtaining property by deception. It is being handled by Team 4 of the Sau Mau Ping district crime unit. No one had been arrested. Police reminded the public that the offence carries a maximum sentence of 14 years' imprisonment.

zh.headline: 六旬婦報稱虛擬貨幣投資被騙2150萬
zh.dek: 警方指她周六報案，4月至9月多次轉帳，平台曾要求交保證金以證明帳戶未涉洗黑錢。
body: 一名60歲女子周六向警方報案，指自己在網上虛擬貨幣投資中損失約2150萬元。《香港01》及《東方日報》報道。
報道指，她早前在網上平台認識一名自稱投資專家的人，其後被引到一個虛擬網站投資加密貨幣。平台其後要求她提交保證金，以證明投資帳戶沒有被用作洗黑錢。她在4月14日至9月22日期間多次轉帳到指定戶口，其後懷疑受騙才報案。
警方將案件列為「以欺騙手段取得財產」，由秀茂坪警區刑事調查隊第四隊跟進，暫未有人被捕。警方提醒，該罪行一經定罪最高可判監14年。
